skills.name: Market system: price signals and enterprise

note.text: A market system relies substantially on private decisions and exchange to allocate resources. Prices communicate information about willingness to buy and the conditions of supply. Firms respond to expected costs and revenue, while consumers choose within their budgets. Profit is revenue minus cost, not revenue alone. Competition can encourage attention to price and quality, but markets operate within institutions and rules. A market system does not mean that every seller succeeds or that every person can afford every good.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A market system relies substantially on private decisions and exchange to allocate resources. Prices communicate information about willingness to buy and the conditions of supply. Firms respond to expected costs and revenue, while consumers choose within their budgets. Profit is revenue minus cost, not revenue alone. Competition can encourage attention to price and quality, but markets operate within institutions and rules. A market system does not mean that every seller succeeds or that every person can afford every good.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: At a Douala market, buyers can compare sellers and decide whether a basket is worth its price. A trader considers how much the stock costs and what buyers will pay. A higher selling price is not automatically a higher profit if costs also rise. This classroom example explains an incentive; it is not advice about how to invest money.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Separate the consumer's choice from the producer's decision. Identify revenue and cost before calculating profit. Look for alternatives when discussing competition. Do not treat an expectation of profit as a guarantee that the business will earn it.
